title: Traction ladders: request bounty dossier
content:
Purpose and framing
-------------------
Compact synthesis of field asks collected Mar–Apr 2027 across enterprise accounts. Organized as "traction ladders": small easy wins that improve adoption and higher-effort changes that unlock new workload classes. Goal: give product & infra a runnable bounty list with clear owners, impact hypotheses, and quick validation probes.

How this was assembled
----------------------
- Sources: frontline CS notes, three customer interviews (FinRegCo, AdTechInc, PlatformPeople), Slack threads #cs-requests, and runtime error logs (spikes Apr 3–9).
- Method: grouped asks by where they appear in the customer journey (onboard, pilot scale, production), then scored for effort (LOE) and expected adoption lift.

Top-level signal (one-line)
-------------------------
Customers want predictable latency and straightforward knobs to avoid tail regressions: low-effort UX/ops changes repeatedly beat heavy model changes for adoption in the next 90 days.

Priority bounty items (ranked)
-----------------------------
1) Route-level latency baseline display (LOE: 1–2 days; Impact: high)
   - What: show p50/p95 token latency per route in Console (last 24h + 7d trend).
   - Why: repeated asks from PlatformPeople and AdTechInc — they need SLA evidence for internal procurement.
   - Hypothesis: visibility reduces support tickets by 30% and speeds up enterprise sign-off.
   - Probe: add a temporary widget and measure support ticket volume over 30 days.
   - Owner: Product (Marco) + Observability (Riley). Jira: JIRA-INF-2123.

2) KV cache warm-stats and recommended TTLs (LOE: 2–3w; Impact: medium-high)
   - What: runtime exposes per-model warm-hit%, 95th miss latency, and a suggested TTL slider in Console that precomputes cost vs latency trade-off.
   - Why: FinRegCo reported frequent cold-start chatter causing inconsistent per-call cost.
   - Hypothesis: guidance improves cache utilization and lowers per-token cost by 12–18% for chat-heavy workloads.
   - Probe: enable an opt-in A/B for 5 pilot customers and track cost delta.
   - Owner: Serving-runtime + Optimize. Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-proto/pull/98.

3) Graceful fallback policy editor (LOE: 3–4w; Impact: high)
   - What: allow product teams to define ordered fallback chains (e.g., quantized variant -> regional fallback -> hosted small model).
   - Why: multiple customers had outages when a single region had transient lag; manual workarounds exist now.
   - Hypothesis: automated fallbacks reduce page incidents and keep 95% of traffic successful during partial outages.
   - Probe: implement feature flag for a single customer; measure error budget usage over 2 weeks.
   - Owner: Platform-engineering + Serving-runtime.

Low-effort wins (1–3 days)
-------------------------
- CLI: add --region flag to the healthcheck tool + clearer exit codes (DevOps asks).
- Docs: quick note on prompt truncation behavior for embeddings (customer confusion observed).
- Console: expose last-failure reason for single requests (helps CS triage).
- Temp workaround: script to backfill KV-cache metrics from logs for customers with short retention.
Owners: DevEx, Docs, Observability.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim where possible)
------------------------------------------------------
- "We can demo Redwood's throughput, but finance wants hard numbers on latency distribution before committing." — FinRegCo platform lead.
- "When the model is slow, we don't know whether to scale GPUs or tweak the prompt — need a short checklist." — AdTechInc SRE.
- "We had a few 'ghost' cost spikes that weren't obviously tied to a change; visibility would have saved dozens of support hours." — PlatformPeople ops.

Risk flags / non-functional concerns
----------------------------------
- Data sensitivity: exposing per-route stats for private deployments must respect VPC-only dashboards (sensitive customers). Add gating.
- Billing telemetry: route-level baselines require linking billing IDs; need legal sign-off for exposing invoices.
- Implementation risk: KV cache instrumentation may add overhead if sampled incorrectly; plan a low-overhead telemetry mode.

Open questions (we should resolve before big work)
------------------------------------------------
- Do we have a single internal source-of-truth for route <-> billing_id mapping? (If no, engineering will need to add mapping.)
- Should fallback editor be managed in Console or via infra-as-code manifests? (CS prefers Console; infra team prefers IaC.)
- What privacy guardrails required for shared-hosted vs private deployments?

Suggested near-term roadmap (90d lens)
--------------------------------------
- Week 0–2: ship Route-level latency baseline widget (temporary UI) + docs update. Measure ticket volume.
- Week 2–6: small CLI fixes, last-failure reason, pilot KV cache stats for 3 customers.
- Week 6–12: gated rollout of fallback policy editor behind feature flag; start formal performance tests.

Metrics to watch (for each probe)
--------------------------------
- Support ticket delta (category: performance)
- Per-route p95 token latency change
- KV cache hit% and cost per 1k tokens
- Incident count and mean time to recover (MTTR) for regional degradations

Action items (owners + due dates)
--------------------------------
- Marco: prototype latency widget and wireframe by 2027-04-20.
- Riley: configure a 30-day ticket tag for performance issues; live by 2027-04-18.
- Emily: draft KV-cache pilot plan and consent wording for customers by 2027-04-25.
- Aisha: coordinate pilot recruitment and customer comms; initial outreach by 2027-04-16.

Follow-ups and communication plan
--------------------------------
- Send this dossier to: #cs, #product-hosted-api, #eng-serving-runtime by EOD 2027-04-14.
- Schedule 30-min sync (CS x Product x Observability) week of 2027-04-18 to assign tickets.
- Update Confluence with measured probe results and a decision log after each 30-day probe.

Notes to reviewers (quick)
------------------------
- This is intentionally prescriptive: the team asked for a short bounty list rather than a long wishlist. Expect iteration.
- If you disagree with a priority, flag it inline and suggest an evidence-based swap (sample size, revenue linkage).

Appendix: quick asks backlog (for triage if we have slack capacity)
----------------------------------------------------------------
- Per-API key quota chart per project.
- Prompt-level telemetry sample for rare failure repro.
- Auto-generated suggested quantization profile for models with median seq_len < 512.

End of dossier.
